claims.claim: In 2018 about 55% of the world's population lived in urban areas, projected to rise to 68% by 2050, according to the UN DESA 2018 Revision of World Urbanization Prospects.

Urbanization plus population growth could add about 2.5 billion people to urban areas by 2050, with close to 90% of that increase in Asia and Africa; India, China, and Nigeria together account for 35% of the projected urban growth from 2018 to 2050.

UN Sustainable Development Goal 11 is to 'make cities and human settlements inclusive, safe, resilient and sustainable', with targets covering adequate housing, sustainable transport, reduced per-capita environmental impact (air quality and waste), and access to green public spaces.

The urban heat island effect makes U.S. cities warmer than surrounding areas, roughly 1-7 degrees F higher during the day and about 2-5 degrees F higher at night, driven by impervious surfaces, loss of vegetation, heat-absorbing materials, urban geometry, and waste heat.

Green infrastructure manages stormwater where it falls using vegetated and permeable features such as green roofs, rain gardens/bioretention, permeable pavement, and bioswales, in contrast to gray infrastructure (pipes and drains) that moves runoff away.

EPA's smart growth is an approach of development and conservation strategies expressed in ten principles, including mixing land uses, compact building design, walkable neighborhoods, a range of housing choices, a variety of transportation choices, and preserving open space.

Compact, walkable urban form is strongly correlated with lower greenhouse-gas emissions because co-located density reduces transport demand and building thermal loss, so dense cities can have lower per-capita footprints; avoiding sprawl is a necessary decarbonization condition.

conflictingEvidence.issue: Whether cities are net good or bad for the environment
positions: Cities concentrate consumption, pollution, and heat, so their absolute footprint is large
On a per-capita basis dense urban living tends to lower transport and building emissions relative to sprawl
conflictingEvidence.resolution: Both hold: absolute urban impact is large while per-capita impact of compact form is typically lower. The lesson states the per-capita point and attributes it to IPCC AR6 WGIII, and does not claim cities are unqualified environmental goods.

unsupportedExistingClaims: The generated draft contained only generic placeholder text ('Sustainable Cities is a foundational concept... introduces its meaning') with no substantive, sourced claims.
correctionsNeeded: Replaced boilerplate definition and vocabulary with sourced, specific content on urbanization data, urban form, green infrastructure, heat islands, smart growth, and SDG 11.

sourceRecords.title: 68% of the world population projected to live in urban areas by 2050 (2018 Revision of World Urbanization Prospects)
sourceRecords.provider: United Nations Department of Economic and Social Affairs (UN DESA), Population Division
sourceRecords.notes: Source of the 55% (2018) to 68% (2050) urban-share figures, the +2.5 billion urban dwellers by 2050 (~90% in Asia and Africa), and the India/China/Nigeria 35% share of projected growth. Read the UN DESA news page directly.

sourceRecords.title: Goal 11: Make cities and human settlements inclusive, safe, resilient and sustainable
sourceRecords.provider: United Nations, Department of Economic and Social Affairs (Sustainable Development Goals)
sourceRecords.notes: Official title and targets of SDG 11 (11.1 housing, 11.2 transport, 11.6 environmental impact/air quality/waste, 11.7 green public space). Adopted 2015 as part of the 2030 Agenda. Target wording quoted minimally with attribution.

sourceRecords.title: Learn About Heat Islands
sourceRecords.notes: Definition and causes of the urban heat island effect and the 1-7 degrees F daytime / 2-5 degrees F nighttime temperature-difference figures for U.S. urban areas; roofs can reach up to 66 degrees F above air temperature.

sourceRecords.title: About Smart Growth
sourceRecords.notes: Definition of smart growth and the ten smart growth principles (mix land uses; compact building design; range of housing; walkable neighborhoods; sense of place; preserve open space; direct development to existing communities; transportation choices; predictable/fair/cost-effective decisions; community collaboration), developed with the Smart Growth Network.

sourceRecords.title: Types of Green Infrastructure
sourceRecords.notes: Green infrastructure captures and manages rainwater where it falls using rain gardens/bioretention, permeable pavement, bioswales, green roofs, and urban tree canopy; contrasts with gray (piped) stormwater infrastructure. Supports stormwater and cooling co-benefits.

sourceRecords.title: IPCC AR6 Working Group III, Chapter 8: Urban Systems and Other Settlements
sourceRecords.notes: AR6 WGIII (2022): compact, walkable urban form is strongly correlated with low GHG emissions; co-located density reduces transport demand and building thermal loss; avoiding sprawl is a necessary decarbonization condition. Supports the lower per-capita footprint point.
